It determines the triangle's bounding box and checks for overlap with Sparse Grid (SG) voxel centers in the yz plane.
It derives the yz range of level-0 tiles, sets up edge functions, and loops over tiles to check for overlap.
If an active tile is found, it loops over 4x4 SG voxel columns, projects centers onto the triangle plane to find the first voxel to flip, and uses atomic XOR operations to flip voxels in the column.
Finest-level voxels are stored only near the boundary, while uniform interior/exterior regions use coarser-level voxels.

In the worst case (highly detailed mesh), it approaches $O(V)$ where $V$ is the number of voxels.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the number of active nodes in the octree.
